review.summary: Round 2 reviews b94e85c after the rebase onto main at 237cc5e: the F record with the round 1 fixes, a runbook 2.1 warning and status-line updates in AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, README.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, ADR-013 and two QA checklists. Of the 13 round 1 findings, 8 are fixed and F-001, F-002, F-009 and F-011 are accepted risks with the accepting role and date recorded; F-012 stays open because the retention decision names no role. The status-line edits match the F record, every added link and anchor resolves and no forbidden data is recorded. The new findings are low or informational documentation gaps: a stale architecture diagram, decision and statement rows still labelled Verified (F), ADR-013 and DEPLOYMENT.md silent on the accepted GitHub deviations, the runbook label table out of step with the record, and contradictory admin-bypass wording. None blocks the release.

findings.summary: The authentication topology diagram still says the rollout and activation are pending F.
findings.rationale: This change updates every textual status to say F performed the rollout, ARCHITECTURE.md embeds the generated diagram, and AGENTS.md requires the PlantUML source and generated SVG to be updated when a diagram is affected.
findings.recommendation: Update both labels to the F result and regenerate the SVG.

findings.summary: Several rows that record a role's decision, acknowledgement or own statement are still labelled Verified (F).
findings.rationale: The new label table defines Recorded as a role's decision and Reported as a role's own statement, and the root key holder row was relabelled on that basis, but the UpCloud account holder, its two-factor authentication, the recovery path acknowledgement, the shared Entra coupling acknowledgement, the TASK-059B scope decision and the failure-reporting confirmation keep Verified (F).
findings.recommendation: Relabel the decisions and acknowledgements as Recorded and the role statements as Reported, or keep Verified (F) only for an observed part.

findings.summary: ADR-013 and DEPLOYMENT.md still describe environment secrets limited to main and a protected main as in place, without pointing to the accepted deviations.
findings.rationale: Production uses repository secrets and main protection that is not independently verified, both accepted deviations whose reassessment before adding a collaborator is recorded only in the F record, while ADR-013 ranks above QA records and is what a repository admin adding a collaborator would read.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-sentence pointer to the F record's deviations and the collaborator trigger in ADR-013's GitHub-side controls and in DEPLOYMENT.md's environment section; whether a lasting deviation needs an ADR amendment is a human decision.

findings.summary: The runbook's label table, which says it lists the labels of the runbook and the F record, no longer matches the F record.
findings.rationale: The F record now words Reported differently and adds Recorded, Not performed and Accepted deviation, and the runbook will be reused for later releases.
findings.recommendation: Add the three labels and the new Reported wording to the runbook table, or point the table to the F record's.

findings.summary: The source-delivery acceptance item says the admin bypass is reported by the repository admin, while the 2.2 row and the failure log say it is not known.
findings.rationale: No bypass value is recorded anywhere, so the qualifier contradicts the rows it links to.
findings.recommendation: Say the settings were stated as configured by the repository admin, are not independently verified and the bypass value is not known.

prior_finding_dispositions.rationale: The 2.2 row is an Accepted deviation and a failure-log row records that the product owner, as repository admin, accepted the unverified main protection on 2026-10-01; the acceptance item is qualified and the reassessment is a follow-up.

A failure-log row records the approval preceding the freeze and the scope confirmation following the deployment, accepted by the main developer on 2026-11-02; section 3 and the acceptance items point to it.
AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, ADR-013, README.md and two QA checklists now say F performed the first rollout, consistent with the F record; the diagram is tracked as a new finding.
The four named rows are now Not performed, Reported and Tested (E); similar decision rows are tracked as a new finding.
The label table defines Recorded, Not performed and Accepted deviation with a pointer to the failure log, and the status note and recording rule mention them.
The hardening, baseline and smoke acceptance items carry qualifiers; the activation-gate wording matches deploy-release.
The failure-log row now refers to 2.2 step 6.
Failure-log rows now cover the unwatched build resources and the late smoke item 5.

The record says the production environment exists and its deployment-branch setting was not observed; the main developer takes its main-only use as known, consistent with the workflow's main-only condition, and the collaborator reassessment is a follow-up.
Runbook 2.1 warns about the stateless firewall and links to the record's rule set, and the record states the IPv4 and IPv6 scope of TCP 22, 80 and 443.
The 2.1 row states that UFW stays the effective filter for reply packets, the rule set was agreed by the product owner, and limiting the reply rules is a recorded follow-up.
The restore evidence file name is recorded in section 5 step 9 and the release record.
